Embedded systems & RTL

Microcontroller Peripherals and Bare-Metal C

Planned notes on non-blocking firmware architecture, timers, interrupts, PWM, ADC, and serial buses across embedded microcontrollers.

To be continued…

Planned scope

This planned series examines bare-metal C and C++ firmware patterns on microcontrollers such as Arduino and Silicon Labs EFM8, focusing on interrupt-driven sensing, hardware timers, software and PCA PWM, SPI display driving, and deterministic non-blocking control loops.

Draft outline

This is a structured draft. Each section will be completed with measured results, commands, and evidence as the work is carried out.

Non-blocking architecture

  • Design a deterministic main loop with explicit state.
  • Avoid blocking delays in sensing and actuation paths.
  • Record timing budgets and worst-case paths.

Timers and interrupts

  • Configure hardware timers for periodic work.
  • Keep interrupt handlers short and predictable.
  • Measure jitter and missed events.

PWM, ADC, and motion

  • Implement software and hardware PWM outputs.
  • Sample analog inputs with defined resolution and timing.
  • Drive a motor stage with safe limits.

Serial peripherals

  • Write SPI, UART, and I2C drivers for the target MCU.
  • Verify bus timing with a logic analyzer.
  • Document error handling and recovery.

Testing and references

  • Record expected outputs for each peripheral.
  • Keep board-specific pin maps with the code.
  • Link the MCU reference manual and project sources.

Topics to cover

  • Non-blocking control loops and scheduling
  • Interrupts and hardware timers
  • PWM motor control and ADC sampling
  • SPI, UART, and I2C peripheral drivers
  • Bare-metal C/C++ on ARM, AVR, and 8051
